title: Fix with a general rule
statement: Fix a reported judging failure with a general rule, and keep the reported item's details, and rules for a single standard, out of the general rubric.
detail: The evaluator repository's working rules say to generalise from a reported example and never paste its item text, answer choices, IDs or issue numbers into prompts, rubrics, evaluators, tests or code unless the requirement is about that literal content (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/AGENTS.md`). A regression test for issue 397 keeps rules for single substandards out of the standardised-test overlays, because that guidance comes from the curriculum service at run time (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/tests/test_sat_overlay_no_substandard_rules.py`).
against: Several audits are still tied to narrow content, such as one that fires when a stem names a wild animal species by its common name and one for fill-in answers that are geographic reference lines (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/closed_ended_evaluation.txt`, lines 63 and 162).

evidence.quote: When fixing an issue, generalize from the reported example. Do not paste the issue's exact example, item text, answer choices, IDs, issue numbers, or attachment-specific content into production prompts, rubrics, evaluators, tests, or code unless the requirement is explicitly about that literal content.
Substandard-level guidance is owned by the curriculum repo and delivered at runtime through the Curriculum API.
